items.title: God’s Wise Mercy
items.summary: The good news is that God himself has decreed a way to satisfy the demands of his justice without condemning the whole human race.

items.title: Our Good Is God’s Delight
items.summary: All the omnipotent energy that drives the heart of God to pursue his own glory also drives him to satisfy the hearts of those who seek their joy in him.

items.title: We Wait, He Works
items.summary: Be freed from the burden of bearing your own load. Let God do that work. God loves to show his God-ness by working for us.

items.title: The Happy God
items.summary: When we share in the happiness of God, we share in the very pleasure that the Father has in the Son.

items.title: Justice Will Be Done
items.summary: When you lay down the burden of vengeance, God will pick it up.

items.title: Joy Unbound
items.summary: Imagine being able to enjoy what is most enjoyable with unbounded energy and passion forever. One day, God’s delight in his Son will be in us.

items.title: Absolute, Sovereign, Almighty Love
items.summary: God does not need us. Instead, his infinite self-sufficiency spills over in love to us who need him.

items.title: The Marriage Miracle That Takes Time
items.summary: Loving our spouses for better or worse includes loving them through their spiritual apathy. Pastor John gives ten encouragements for the weary.

items.title: When You’re Not Sorry
items.summary: When someone confronts you wrongly, should you apologize? Pastor John encourages humility and reconciliation without giving in to emotional manipulation.

items.title: The Gospel Before Jesus Died
items.summary: Did Jesus preach the gospel before his death and resurrection? Pastor John calls us to a deeper understanding of God as Creator and King, and Jesus as Lord and Savior.

items.title: The Perils of a Quick Fix
items.summary: How can we witness to those who just want a quick fix? Pastor John presses home the shocking reality of eternity and the astounding love of Jesus.

items.title: When I’m Too Weak to Be Productive
items.summary: Can a disabled mother model the Proverbs 31 woman? Pastor John describes the gift of a heart that hopes in God’s steadfast love.

items.title: Six Traits of a Forgettable Sermon
items.summary: Rigorous exposition isn’t at odds with engaging preaching. Pastor John encourages pastors to work for creativity when technical, abstract sermons feel easier.

items.title: Resting Grace
items.summary: One trait or quality of a supernaturally changed heart is peace. There’s a difference between a supernaturally changed heart and a morally restrained heart. The marks of a supernaturally changed heart are sometimes called the fruit of the Spirit. They’re listed a number of places in the New Testament. And peace is…

items.title: Befriending Grace
items.summary: Every religion in the world gives you a list of virtuous behaviors. But the New Testament gives you something different. It does give you a list, but it’s of aspects of how a supernaturally, grace-changed heart shows itself. The apostle Paul says it’s possible to do all the morally virtuous behavior without any love…

items.title: Forgiving Grace
items.summary: Morally virtuous behavior can arise out of a heart that hasn’t actually been supernaturally changed. For example, in traditional moral training, we teach people to be honest by using a motive of fear and insecurity. But only for a heart that feels absolutely loved is lying unnecessary and unnatural. It’s only an…

items.title: Love and the Practical Graces
items.summary: The city of Corinth was a place of commerce. Nobody went there except to be successful. It was built from scratch just a few decades before Paul’s letter was written. There were not old families and traditions. This was a place that attracted an unusually resourceful, talented, ambitious, intense kind of person. And…

items.title: Secret of Our Discontent (Open Forum)
items.summary: This talk was given by Dr. Timothy Keller at Redeemer Presbyterian Church on November 6, 1994. Series: Redeemer Open Forums. Today's episode is brought to you by Gospel in Life, the site for all sermons, books, study guides and resources from Timothy Keller and Redeemer Presbyterian Church. If you've enjoyed…

items.title: Paul’s Prayer (Part 2)
items.summary: This sermon was preached by Dr. Timothy Keller at Redeemer Presbyterian Church on August 29, 1993. Series: Salvation From the Outside In. Scripture: Ephesians 3:14-21. Today's podcast is brought to you by Gospel in Life, the site for all sermons, books, study guides and resources from Timothy Keller and Redeemer…

items.title: Life-Changing Prayer
items.summary: As you bring your requests to God, don't just seek a change in circumstances, ask Him to transform your heart.

items.title: Praying Through the Silence
items.summary: In the moments when God seems silent, keep praying and let His presence bring you peace.

items.title: Why Isn’t God Speaking?
items.summary: There is a purpose in God's silence—He wants to teach us and bring our focus back to Him.

items.title: When God Is Silent
items.summary: An unanswered prayer doesn't mean God is ignoring you. Even in the silence, He is still at work.

items.title: Our Helper in Prayer
items.summary: Sometimes praying feels hard. But we can pray with confidence, knowing the Spirit intercedes for us.

items.title: An Ever-Present Helper
items.summary: Whatever today holds, God has given every believer direct access to His help through the Holy Spirit.

items.title: Spiritual Maturity
items.summary: Facing hardship allows us to deepen our reliance on God.

items.title: Praise Without Ceasing (1 Chronicles 23:30)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 1 Chronicles 23:30, David Platt teaches us to praise God in every circumstance. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Humble Leadership (1 Chronicles 21:14)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 1 Chronicles 21:14, David Platt calls us to humble leadership, reminding us that our sin affects those we lead. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Strength to Serve (1 Chronicles 19:13)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 1 Chronicles 19:13, David Platt urges us to seek the good of others through God’s strength in us. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Undeserved Grace (1 Chronicles 17:16)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 1 Chronicles 17:16, David Platt reminds us that God gives his grace even when we don't deserve it. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Seek the Lord (1 Chronicles 16:10–11)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 1 Chronicles 16:10–11, David Platt illustrates what it means to seek God truly. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Living by the Word (1 Chronicles 15:13–15)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 1 Chronicles 15:13–15, David Platt challenges Christians to consider if they are honoring God with their lives. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: The Seriousness of Sin (1 Chronicles 13:10)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 1 Chronicles 13:10, David Platt urges us to respond to sin with sober-mindedness. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: You Can Know God But Never Master Him
items.summary: In this episode, Costi Hinn explains what it means for God to be incomprehensible. God is infinitely greater than our minds can comprehend, yet He has made Himself truly knowable through His Word and ultimately through Jesus Christ.

items.title: Your View of God Shapes Everything
items.summary: You may not deny God, but do you diminish Him? In this episode, Costi Hinn examines how a small or distorted view of God can shape the way we live, exposing the gap between what we confess about God and how we actually function day to day.

items.title: No One Is Above God
items.summary: The name El Elyon means “God Most High,” declaring God’s absolute supremacy over everyone and everything. In this final episode of the Names of God series, Costi Hinn explains what it means to live with the perspective that God is sovereign, owns everything, and answers to no one.

items.title: Why Is God Jealous?
items.summary: God’s jealousy is not sinful, insecure, or possessive. It is His holy zeal for His glory and His covenant relationship with His people. In this episode, Costi Hinn explains what it means for God to be El Qanna, the jealous God, and why He refuses to share the worship that belongs exclusively to Him.

items.title: God Is Stronger Than Your Circumstances
items.summary: In this episode, Costi Hinn explores El Gibbor, the Mighty God, and what this name reveals about the strength, sovereignty, and victory of God. When life feels bigger than you, remember: you don’t have to be strong enough. Your God is.
